"PROJECT ASTRA: REBIRTH

A Premium 3D Anime Open-World Action RPG

Act as an experienced AAA game development studio consisting of game directors, 3D environment artists, gameplay programmers, combat designers, AI engineers, animation specialists, sound designers and QA engineers.

Create a beautiful, fully playable 3D anime-style open-world action RPG called ASTRA: REBIRTH.

The objective is to create a substantial game with impressive visuals, responsive gameplay, immersive exploration and deep combat mechanics.

IMPORTANT:
Do not create a static 3D scene or a simple walking simulator. Build an actual interactive game with functional systems.

1. GAME WORLD

Create a large interconnected fantasy world with these regions:

1. Aetheria – A beautiful starting kingdom with villages, forests and mountains.
2. Sakura Valley – A Japanese-inspired region with cherry blossom trees and temples.
3. Ember Desert – A dangerous desert with ancient ruins.
4. Frostfall – A snowy mountain region with frozen lakes.
5. Celestial City – A futuristic fantasy city with advanced architecture.
6. Abyss Realm – A mysterious dark region containing powerful enemies.

Each region should contain unique environments, NPCs, enemies, secrets, exploration rewards and quests.

Use seamless exploration where technically possible. Otherwise use polished transitions between regions.

2. PLAYER AND CHARACTER SYSTEM

Create an anime-style 3D protagonist with:

- Detailed character model.
- Smooth running and walking animations.
- Jumping and double jumping.
- Sprinting and dodging.
- Climbing and swimming where supported.
- Sword attacks.
- Special abilities.
- Character progression.
- Equipment and customization.

Implement a responsive third-person camera with smooth follow and adjustable sensitivity.

3. ADVANCED COMBAT SYSTEM

Create a satisfying real-time combat system.

Include:

- Light and heavy attacks.
- Weapon combos.
- Charged attacks.
- Air attacks.
- Perfect dodge mechanics.
- Blocking and counterattacks.
- Elemental abilities.
- Ultimate attacks.
- Enemy hit reactions.
- Knockback and damage feedback.
- Critical damage.
- Cinematic finishing effects.

Combat must use real hit detection and damage calculations.

4. ELEMENTAL POWER SYSTEM

Implement five elemental powers:

- Fire: Burning attacks and explosions.
- Ice: Freezing and slowing enemies.
- Lightning: Fast chain attacks.
- Wind: Air manipulation and mobility.
- Shadow: Teleportation and stealth attacks.

Each element must have distinct gameplay abilities, visual effects and upgrade paths.

5. CHARACTER SWITCHING

Create three playable anime characters:

- A sword-wielding warrior.
- A fast dual-blade assassin.
- A powerful elemental mage.

Allow instant character switching during combat.

Each character must have unique animations, combat styles, abilities and ultimate attacks.

6. ENEMY AI

Create different enemy categories:

- Basic soldiers.
- Fast melee enemies.
- Ranged attackers.
- Flying creatures.
- Elite monsters.
- Mini-bosses.
- Massive world bosses.

Implement enemy detection, chasing, attacking, dodging, retreating and reacting to player actions.

7. BOSS BATTLES

Create five unique boss encounters.

Every boss should have:

- A unique 3D model or distinctive visual design.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Special abilities.
- Boss health bar.
- Appropriate animations.
- Victory rewards.

Bosses must be challenging but fair.

8. OPEN-WORLD EXPLORATION

Include:

- Interactive villages.
- NPC conversations.
- Shops and merchants.
- Hidden treasure chests.
- Ancient temples.
- Dungeons.
- Collectibles.
- Fast travel points.
- Exploration challenges.
- Environmental puzzles.
- Dynamic weather.
- Day and night cycle.

9. QUEST AND STORY SYSTEM

Create an original anime-inspired storyline.

The protagonist discovers an ancient power threatening the world.

Include:

- Main storyline.
- Side quests.
- NPC missions.
- Dialogue system.
- Story progression.
- Cinematic events.
- Quest tracking.
- Rewards and achievements.

Do not copy characters or storylines from existing anime or games.

10. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement:

- Experience points.
- Player levels.
- Character upgrades.
- Weapon upgrades.
- Skill trees.
- Elemental upgrades.
- Equipment rarity.
- Collectible materials.
- Reward system.

11. VISUAL QUALITY

Aim for high-quality anime-inspired 3D visuals.

Include:

- Detailed 3D environments.
- Cel-shaded or anime-inspired rendering.
- Beautiful lighting.
- Realistic shadows.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Water reflections where supported.
- Particle effects.
- Magical attack effects.
- Smooth character animations.
- Detailed environments.
- Cinematic camera effects.
- High-quality UI.

Maintain consistent art direction.

12. AUDIO

Include:

- Original background music.
- Environmental sounds.
- Sword attack sounds.
- Magic ability sounds.
- Enemy sounds.
- Boss battle music.
- UI sound effects.

13. USER INTERFACE

Create a professional interface containing:

- Main menu.
- Character selection.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Health and stamina bars.
- Ability buttons.
- Mini-map.
- Boss health bar.
- Settings.
- Pause menu.
- Victory and defeat screens.

14. MOBILE AND PC CONTROLS

Support:

- Keyboard and mouse.
- Third-person camera controls.
- Mobile virtual joystick.
- Attack buttons.
- Jump and dodge buttons.
- Character switching.
- Special ability buttons.

Make the UI responsive to different screen sizes.

15. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

First inspect the available game engine, runtime, rendering capabilities and project structure.

Use the existing supported technology.

Avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized external assets.

Use optimized 3D models, textures, lighting and level-of-detail techniques.

Implement:

- Efficient enemy spawning.
- Collision detection.
- Object pooling where appropriate.
- Optimized world loading.
- Persistent save system.
- Stable game state management.
- Performance monitoring.

Target smooth performance on supported devices.

16. DEVELOPMENT PHASES

Develop the project incrementally:

PHASE 1: Technical foundation, 3D player controller, camera and movement.

PHASE 2: Combat system, weapons, animations and elemental abilities.

PHASE 3: Enemy AI, boss fights and damage systems.

PHASE 4: Open-world environment and exploration.

PHASE 5: NPCs, quests, dialogue and story.

PHASE 6: Character switching, inventory and progression.

PHASE 7: UI, audio, visual effects and polish.

PHASE 8: Save system, optimization and bug fixing.

After every phase, test existing functionality before continuing.

17. FINAL QUALITY REQUIREMENTS

The finished result must be an actual playable 3D anime action RPG.

Do not simulate features using decorative buttons.

Do not leave core mechanics unfinished.

Do not replace gameplay with screenshots or static environments.

Fix broken controls, camera problems, collision errors and gameplay bugs.

If the entire game cannot fit into one generation, build a complete playable vertical slice first, then expand the existing project in stages.

Prioritize functional gameplay, visual quality, stability and optimization.

FINAL GOAL:
Create an impressive anime open-world experience that feels like a professionally developed indie action RPG, with a beautiful world, exciting combat, memorable bosses and satisfying exploration.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub. ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action

live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

"PROJECT ASTRA: REBIRTH

A Premium 3D Anime Open-World Action RPG

Act as an experienced AAA game development studio consisting of game directors, 3D environment artists, gameplay programmers, combat designers, AI engineers, animation specialists, sound designers and QA engineers.

Create a beautiful, fully playable 3D anime-style open-world action RPG called ASTRA: REBIRTH.

The objective is to create a substantial game with impressive visuals, responsive gameplay, immersive exploration and deep combat mechanics.

IMPORTANT:
Do not create a static 3D scene or a simple walking simulator. Build an actual interactive game with functional systems.

1. GAME WORLD

Create a large interconnected fantasy world with these regions:

1. Aetheria – A beautiful starting kingdom with villages, forests and mountains.
2. Sakura Valley – A Japanese-inspired region with cherry blossom trees and temples.
3. Ember Desert – A dangerous desert with ancient ruins.
4. Frostfall – A snowy mountain region with frozen lakes.
5. Celestial City – A futuristic fantasy city with advanced architecture.
6. Abyss Realm – A mysterious dark region containing powerful enemies.

Each region should contain unique environments, NPCs, enemies, secrets, exploration rewards and quests.

Use seamless exploration where technically possible. Otherwise use polished transitions between regions.

2. PLAYER AND CHARACTER SYSTEM

Create an anime-style 3D protagonist with:

- Detailed character model.
- Smooth running and walking animations.
- Jumping and double jumping.
- Sprinting and dodging.
- Climbing and swimming where supported.
- Sword attacks.
- Special abilities.
- Character progression.
- Equipment and customization.

Implement a responsive third-person camera with smooth follow and adjustable sensitivity.

3. ADVANCED COMBAT SYSTEM

Create a satisfying real-time combat system.

Include:

- Light and heavy attacks.
- Weapon combos.
- Charged attacks.
- Air attacks.
- Perfect dodge mechanics.
- Blocking and counterattacks.
- Elemental abilities.
- Ultimate attacks.
- Enemy hit reactions.
- Knockback and damage feedback.
- Critical damage.
- Cinematic finishing effects.

Combat must use real hit detection and damage calculations.

4. ELEMENTAL POWER SYSTEM

Implement five elemental powers:

- Fire: Burning attacks and explosions.
- Ice: Freezing and slowing enemies.
- Lightning: Fast chain attacks.
- Wind: Air manipulation and mobility.
- Shadow: Teleportation and stealth attacks.

Each element must have distinct gameplay abilities, visual effects and upgrade paths.

5. CHARACTER SWITCHING

Create three playable anime characters:

- A sword-wielding warrior.
- A fast dual-blade assassin.
- A powerful elemental mage.

Allow instant character switching during combat.

Each character must have unique animations, combat styles, abilities and ultimate attacks.

6. ENEMY AI

Create different enemy categories:

- Basic soldiers.
- Fast melee enemies.
- Ranged attackers.
- Flying creatures.
- Elite monsters.
- Mini-bosses.
- Massive world bosses.

Implement enemy detection, chasing, attacking, dodging, retreating and reacting to player actions.

7. BOSS BATTLES

Create five unique boss encounters.

Every boss should have:

- A unique 3D model or distinctive visual design.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Special abilities.
- Boss health bar.
- Appropriate animations.
- Victory rewards.

Bosses must be challenging but fair.

8. OPEN-WORLD EXPLORATION

Include:

- Interactive villages.
- NPC conversations.
- Shops and merchants.
- Hidden treasure chests.
- Ancient temples.
- Dungeons.
- Collectibles.
- Fast travel points.
- Exploration challenges.
- Environmental puzzles.
- Dynamic weather.
- Day and night cycle.

9. QUEST AND STORY SYSTEM

Create an original anime-inspired storyline.

The protagonist discovers an ancient power threatening the world.

Include:

- Main storyline.
- Side quests.
- NPC missions.
- Dialogue system.
- Story progression.
- Cinematic events.
- Quest tracking.
- Rewards and achievements.

Do not copy characters or storylines from existing anime or games.

10. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement:

- Experience points.
- Player levels.
- Character upgrades.
- Weapon upgrades.
- Skill trees.
- Elemental upgrades.
- Equipment rarity.
- Collectible materials.
- Reward system.

11. VISUAL QUALITY

Aim for high-quality anime-inspired 3D visuals.

Include:

- Detailed 3D environments.
- Cel-shaded or anime-inspired rendering.
- Beautiful lighting.
- Realistic shadows.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Water reflections where supported.
- Particle effects.
- Magical attack effects.
- Smooth character animations.
- Detailed environments.
- Cinematic camera effects.
- High-quality UI.

Maintain consistent art direction.

12. AUDIO

Include:

- Original background music.
- Environmental sounds.
- Sword attack sounds.
- Magic ability sounds.
- Enemy sounds.
- Boss battle music.
- UI sound effects.

13. USER INTERFACE

Create a professional interface containing:

- Main menu.
- Character selection.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Health and stamina bars.
- Ability buttons.
- Mini-map.
- Boss health bar.
- Settings.
- Pause menu.
- Victory and defeat screens.

14. MOBILE AND PC CONTROLS

Support:

- Keyboard and mouse.
- Third-person camera controls.
- Mobile virtual joystick.
- Attack buttons.
- Jump and dodge buttons.
- Character switching.
- Special ability buttons.

Make the UI responsive to different screen sizes.

15. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

First inspect the available game engine, runtime, rendering capabilities and project structure.

Use the existing supported technology.

Avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized external assets.

Use optimized 3D models, textures, lighting and level-of-detail techniques.

Implement:

- Efficient enemy spawning.
- Collision detection.
- Object pooling where appropriate.
- Optimized world loading.
- Persistent save system.
- Stable game state management.
- Performance monitoring.

Target smooth performance on supported devices.

16. DEVELOPMENT PHASES

Develop the project incrementally:

PHASE 1: Technical foundation, 3D player controller, camera and movement.

PHASE 2: Combat system, weapons, animations and elemental abilities.

PHASE 3: Enemy AI, boss fights and damage systems.

PHASE 4: Open-world environment and exploration.

PHASE 5: NPCs, quests, dialogue and story.

PHASE 6: Character switching, inventory and progression.

PHASE 7: UI, audio, visual effects and polish.

PHASE 8: Save system, optimization and bug fixing.

After every phase, test existing functionality before continuing.

17. FINAL QUALITY REQUIREMENTS

The finished result must be an actual playable 3D anime action RPG.

Do not simulate features using decorative buttons.

Do not leave core mechanics unfinished.

Do not replace gameplay with screenshots or static environments.

Fix broken controls, camera problems, collision errors and gameplay bugs.

If the entire game cannot fit into one generation, build a complete playable vertical slice first, then expand the existing project in stages.

Prioritize functional gameplay, visual quality, stability and optimization.

FINAL GOAL:
Create an impressive anime open-world experience that feels like a professionally developed indie action RPG, with a beautiful world, exciting combat, memorable bosses and satisfying exploration.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, or a polished vertical slice if the full scope is too large.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at completion.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Inspected the UI markup and existing model and input APIs.

### Active
- Implement the world module, then integrate gameplay systems and UI.
- Verify the game runs and exercise core gameplay; no testing results have been reported.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement a world module using the existing Three.js utilities and procedural props.
2. Create `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, and progression.
3. Run the project, test core controls and gameplay, and fix errors.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, UI markup, import map, and `src/game.js` entry point.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `vendor/`: Locally vendored Three.js modules and supporting assets.

## Important Context
- `src/game.js` and a world module are still missing; `index.html` references `src/game.js`.
- Model exports include `createHero`, `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, and world props including `createTorii`, `createLantern`, `createCrystal`, `createChest`, and `createCrystalWaypoint`.
- `Input` exposes keyboard, mouse, touch action, joystick, and pointer-lock interfaces.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at completion.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, a village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected UI markup, model/world APIs, and input/audio/particle interfaces for gameplay integration.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, and progression.
- Run the project and test core controls and gameplay; fix errors.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, UI markup, import map, and entry point referencing missing `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- Model exports include `createHero`, `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, and world props including `createTorii`, `createLantern`, `createCrystal`, `createChest`, and `createCrystalWaypoint`.
- `CHARACTERS` in `src/models.js` defines Kael, Yumi, and Aria stats; `BOSS_DEFS` defines bosses and locations.
- `Input` exposes keyboard, mouse, touch action, joystick, and pointer-lock interfaces; `AudioEngine` and `ParticleSystem` are available in `src/engine.js`.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the earlier status check.

8:

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at completion.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected markup and APIs needed to integrate gameplay.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, progression, and persistence.
- Run the project and test core controls and gameplay; fix errors.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references missing `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- Model exports include `createHero`, `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, world props, `CHARACTERS`, and `BOSS_DEFS`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`.
- `AudioEngine` and `ParticleSystem` are available in `src/engine.js`.
- No gameplay integration or testing has been performed yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at completion.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected markup, input APIs, model exports, and world data needed for gameplay integration.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, progression, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core controls and gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references missing `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- Model exports include `createHero`, `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, world props, `CHARACTERS`, and `BOSS_DEFS`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`.
- `AudioEngine` and `ParticleSystem` are available in `src/engine.js`.
- Gameplay integration and testing have not yet been performed.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in git status.

- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at completion.

- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

- (none)

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if needed.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use existing technology, avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized assets, and make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, a village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected UI markup, model exports, world data, and input APIs for gameplay integration.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, progression, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core controls and gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references missing `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- `createHero(id)` returns a rig with its root at `rig.rock` (not `rig.root`); it also includes `body` and character animation parts.
- Model exports include `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, world props, `CHARACTERS`, and `BOSS_DEFS`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`.
- `AudioEngine` and `ParticleSystem` are available in `src/engine.js`.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice if needed.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use existing technology, avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized assets, and make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, a village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected UI markup, model exports, world data, and input APIs for gameplay integration.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, progression, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core controls and gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references missing `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.

- `createWorld` places the starting village near `(0,0)` and the Verdant Warden near `(138,-78)`.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use existing technology, avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized assets, and make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, a village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Inspected UI markup, model exports, world data, and input APIs for gameplay integration.

### Active
- Implement `src/game.js` to connect world setup, movement, combat, enemies, exploration, UI, progression, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/game.js`, integrating title/character selection, gameplay, combat, interactions, HUD, progression, and persistence.
2. Run the project and exercise core controls and gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references `src/game.js`.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- `createHero(id)` returns a rig with its root at `rig.rock` (not `rig.root`); it also includes `body` and character animation parts.
- Model exports include `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, `createBossMesh`, world props, `CHARACTERS`, and `BOSS_DEFS`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`; touch input is exposed through `actionPressed()`/`actionDown()`.
- `AudioEngine` and `ParticleSystem` are available in `src/engine.js`.
- `createWorld` places the starting village near `(0,0)` and the Verdant Warden near `(138,-78)`.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e40d998b9ffeLIZRJ0PFhonfge" state="completed">
## Repository status

`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js` does not exist, although `index.html` loads it as an ES module. The findings below describe the available hooks and APIs; they do not establish game-side event handlers or gameplay behavior that would have been implemented there.

## DOM IDs and interaction hooks

`index.html` defines these IDs, grouped by purpose:

- **Canvas/overlays:** `app`, `game-canvas`, `cinema-bars`, `vignette`, `flash`, `slowmo-overlay`
- **HUD:** `hud`, `avatar-glyph`, `hud-char-name`, `hud-level`, `hp-fill`, `hp-text`, `stamina-fill`, `stamina-text`, `xp-fill`, `hud-gold`, `hud-shards`, `hud-xp`, `minimap`, `hud-region`, `hud-time`, `quest-tracker`, `quest-title`, `quest-objective`, `quest-distance`, `party-bar`, `ability-bar`, `boss-wrap`, `boss-title`, `boss-phase`, `boss-fill`, `interaction-prompt`, `interaction-text`, `region-banner`, `region-banner-name`, `region-banner-sub`, `boss-intro`, `boss-intro-name`, `objective-toast`, `damage-layer`, `toast-stack`, `fps-counter`, `reticle`
- **Mobile controls:** `mobile-controls`, `joystick-zone`, `joystick-base`, `joystick-knob`, `mobile-menu`
- **Title/character select:** `title-screen`, `btn-new-game`, `btn-continue`, `continue-label`, `btn-how`, `btn-credits`, `char-select`, `cs-back`
- **Pause/codex:** `pause-menu`, `pause-nav`, `btn-save`, `btn-title`, `pause-title`, `pause-subtitle`, `pause-level`, `pause-gold`, `pause-content`, `pause-close`
- **Dialogue/shop/modal:** `dialogue`, `dlg-glyph`, `dlg-name`, `dlg-role`, `dlg-text`, `dlg-options`, `shop-panel`, `shop-title`, `shop-gold`, `shop-close`, `shop-items`, `modal`, `modal-kicker`, `modal-title`, `modal-body`, `modal-close`
- **Other screens:** `class-card`, `cc-name`, `cc-role`, `ending-screen`, `ending-text`, `ending-stats`, `ending-continue`, `death-screen`, `btn-respawn`, `btn-death-title`, `victory-screen`, `victory-name`, `victory-rewards`, `victory-continue`, `loading`, `load-fill`, `load-text`

Markup interaction hooks:

- Buttons use `data-action`: `attack`, `heavy`, `jump`, `dodge`, `block`, `ability`, `ultimate`, `switch`, `menu`.
- Character-select cards use `data-char`: `kael`, `yumi`, `aria`.
- Pause navigation uses `data-tab`: `inventory`, `equipment`, `skills`, `quests`, `map`, `settings`.
- `Input.bind()` installs pointer handlers for every `[data-action]` element and reads `btn.dataset.action`; the joystick uses `#joystick-zone` and `#joystick-knob`.
- The character-switch hint names keys `1`, `2`, `3`. The dialogue hint says `F / CLICK to continue`; the interaction prompt shows `F`.
- These are markup/input hooks only. With `game.js` absent, the associated game actions and DOM updates cannot be confirmed.

## World construction and entity records

`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js` exports `createWorld(scene)`. It creates a `THREE.Group` world and returns:

```js
{
  world, ground, npcs, enemies, bosses, collectibles, props,
  regions, sun, random, getRegion(x, z)
}
```

`getRegion(x, z)` returns the region with the nearest `x,z` coordinates. Region records have `{ name, sub, color, ground, x, z }`; the names are `AETHERIA`, `SAKURA`, `EMBER`, `FROSTFALL`, and `ABYSS`.

Entity record shapes and initial data:

- **NPCs:** `{ id, name, role, mesh, x, z, kind }`. Initial records are Elder Elara (`id: 'elder'`, `kind: 'elder'`, at `-4,-5`) and the Traveling Merchant (`id: 'merchant'`, `kind: 'merchant'`, at `5,-4`). Their `mesh` is the NPC rig’s `root` group.
- **Enemies:** `{ type, rig, mesh, x, z, hp, maxHp, attack, radius, aggro, cooldown, hitFlash, dead, homeX, homeZ }`. Types spawned are `soldier`, `raider`, `wisp`, `archer`, `brute`, and `elite`. `mesh` is `rig.root`; position is also recorded as `x,z`. Initial HP is 130 for elite, 100 for brute, 55 for wisp, and 68 otherwise; attack is 16 for elite, 13 for brute, and 9 otherwise; radius is 1.15 for brute and 0.75 otherwise; aggro starts at 16.
- **Boss:** one initial record, `{ id, def, rig, mesh, x, z, hp, maxHp, radius, attack, cooldown, hitFlash, active, defeated, phase }`. It uses the Warden definition, starts with `active: false`, `defeated: false`, `phase: 1`, and attack 23.
- **Collectibles:** `{ kind, mesh, x, z, active, label }`. The world creates a waypoint (`kind: 'waypoint'`), a chest (`'chest'`), and starshards (`'shard'`).
- **Props:** a plain array of prop `Object3D`s. It includes placed scenery and the NPC model groups; enemies and the boss have their own arrays.

`world.js` has no entity update functions. The caller would need to update movement, combat/state fields, mesh transforms, collectible activity, and any animated effects.

## `Input` API

In `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/engine.js`, `Input(canvas)` exposes:

- State: `canvas`, `keys`, `just`, `mouseButtons`, `mouseJust`, `look: { x, y }`, `locked`, `joystick: { x, y, active }`, `touchActions`, `touchJust`, and `touchCapable`. `buttons` and `buttonsJust` are also initialized but have no handlers or accessors in this file.
- Methods: `bind()`, `requestLock()`, `exitLock()`, `down(code)`, `pressed(code)`, `mouseDown(b = 0)`, `mousePressed(b = 0)`, `consumeLook()`, `actionDown(a)`, `actionPressed(a)`, `endFrame()`.
- Keyboard methods take `KeyboardEvent.code` strings. `pressed` and the “just” queries are cleared by `endFrame()`.
- Mouse methods use button numbers (default `0` for left mouse). `consumeLook()` returns accumulated `{ x, y }` movement and resets both values.
- Touch action state is populated from `[data-action]`: pointer down marks the action held and just-pressed; pointer up/cancel/leave releases it. The joystick updates normalized `x,y` and `active`, and resets on release/cancel.
- Pointer lock is skipped on touch-capable devices. The canvas requests it on a non-touch left click; mouse movement accumulates while locked or dragging.

## `ParticleSystem` API

`ParticleSystem(scene, max = 1800)` creates a `THREE.Points` system and exposes:

- `emit(o = {})`
- `update(dt)`

`emit` accepts `pos`, `count`, `color`, `spread`, `speed`, `speedVar`, `life`, `lifeVar`, `size`, `sizeVar`, `gravity`, `drag`, `ring`, `dir`, `cone`, `up`, and `color2`. Defaults are `count: 8`, white color, spread `0.4`, speed `2`, speed variation `1`, life `0.7`, life variation `0.3`, size `6`, size variation `3`, gravity `0`, drag `1.5`, `ring: false`, `dir: null`, and `cone: 0`. `pos` defaults to a new `THREE.Vector3()`. Emission reuses slots in a circular buffer; `update(dt)` advances particle motion, gravity/drag, life, alpha, and size.

## Model entity definitions and rig properties

`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js` exports `CHARACTERS`, `BOSS_DEFS`, and constructors including `createHero`, `createNpc`, `createEnemyMesh`, and `createBossMesh`.

Character definitions share the fields `id`, `name`, `role`, `glyph`, `element`, `weapon`, `hp`, `stamina`, `attack`, `defense`, `speed`, `crit`, `critMult`, `colors`, and `title`:

| ID | Element / weapon | HP / stamina | Attack / defense | Speed | Crit / multiplier |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `kael` | Fire / `greatsword` | 150 / 110 | 30 / 12 | 5.5 | 0.12 / 1.8 |
| `yumi` | Lightning / `dual` | 115 / 130 | 24 / 8 | 6.5 | 0.22 / 1.9 |
| `aria` | Ice / `staff` | 125 / 120 | 27 / 9 | 5.2 | 0.16 / 2.0 |

Their color records have `hair`, `hair2`, `skin`, `cloth`, `cloth2`, `accent`, `trim`, and `eye`.

- **Hero rigs** have `{ rock: root, body, def }`, plus animation/model references such as `legL`, `legR`, `kneeL`, `kneeR`, `chestGem`, `hair`, `hairPieces`, arm/elbow/hand references, `weapon`, and `auraRing`. Character-specific extras include Kael’s `scarf`, Yumi’s `pony` and `weapon2`, and Aria’s `orbA`, `orbB`, and `orbC`.
- **NPC rigs** have `root`, `body`, `head`, `armL`, and `armR`.
- **Enemy rigs** include `root`, `body`, and `type`; other rig fields vary by type, including limb, head, weapon/shield, aura, or wisp-core/wing references.
- **Boss definitions** contain `{ id, name, title, hp, level, radius, region, pos, element, arena }`. `BOSS_DEFS` defines `warden`, `shogun`, `wyrm`, `colossus`, and `seraph`. Boss rigs expose `root`, `body`, `def`, with additional anatomy/effect references depending on boss type. `createWorld()` currently instantiates only `warden`.

The file-specific findings are from `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`, `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`, `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/engine.js`, and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`.
</subagent>

- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use existing technology, avoid unnecessary dependencies and oversized assets, and make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell in `index.html`, styling in `src/style.css`, shared utilities and input controls in `src/engine.js`, and procedural models in `src/models.js`.
- Added `src/world.js` with procedural terrain, a village, shrine, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, a boss arena, and distant biome landmarks.
- Created the initial `src/game.js` scaffold with renderer, scene/world setup, game state, hero mounting, journey initialization, and resize handling.

### Active
- Finish `src/game.js`: implement UI wiring, movement, combat, enemy/boss behavior, interactions, progression, persistence, HUD, and render loop.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/game.js` gameplay systems and UI interactions.
2. Run the project and exercise core controls and gameplay; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI markup; entry point references `src/game.js`.
- `src/game.js`: Current gameplay integration scaffold; still incomplete.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and entity placement.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/mobile input.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, boss, and world-prop builders.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

- Repository changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.

- Character definitions are `kael`, `yumi`, and `aria`; their stats are in `CHARACTERS` in `src/models.js`.

The gameplay and UI helper functions referenced there, including `setQuest`, `toast`, and `saveGame`, are not yet implemented.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, styling, shared utilities/input controls, procedural models, and procedural world.
- Implemented renderer, world setup, game state, hero mounting, resize handling, journey restoration, save/load, HUD, minimap, pause-tab content, quest text, and toast scaffolding in `src/game.js`.
- Added gameplay helper functions in `src/game.js` for dialogue, shop, interactions, quests, XP/leveling, enemy/boss damage, combat attacks, and ultimate ability.
- Inspected relevant DOM controls and the `Input` API for integration.

### Active
- Integrate gameplay in `src/game.js`: movement, enemy/boss updates, camera, animation, UI/event wiring, and render loop.
- Test controls, interactions, combat, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire title/character selection, dialogue/shop, pause/death/victory UI, combat/world interactions, and keyboard/mobile events.
2. Implement player movement/animation, enemy and boss behavior, camera updates, and render loop.
3. Check DOM IDs and controls against `index.html` and `src/engine.js`; run the project and test the vertical slice.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Main integration; gameplay helpers exist, but event wiring and update/render loop remain incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for HUD, title/select, pause, dialogue, shop, and ending screens.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain, village, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, and Verdant Warden arena.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/touch input.
- `src/models.js`: Character definitions and procedural hero, enemy, NPC, and boss models.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- `createHero(id)` returns a rig with its root at `rig.rock`; character definitions are in `CHARACTERS` in `src/models.js`.

- Verdant Warden is near `(138,-78)`; world enemies have patrol/home, health, attack, aggro, cooldown, and dead fields.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, styling, shared utilities/input controls, procedural models, and procedural world.
- Implemented renderer, world setup, initial game state, hero mounting, resize handling, journey restoration, save/load, HUD, minimap, pause-tab content, quest text, and toast scaffolding in `src/game.js`.

### Active
- Continue integrating gameplay after `renderPauseTab()` in `src/game.js`.
- Wire title/character selection, dialogue/shop, pause/death/victory UI, combat/world interactions, and keyboard/mobile events.
- Implement player movement/animation, enemy and boss behavior, camera updates, and render loop.
- Test controls, interactions, combat, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/game.js` after `renderPauseTab()` with gameplay helpers and event wiring.
2. Implement movement, combat, enemy/boss updates, camera, and render loop.
3. Run the project and test the vertical slice.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Main integration; currently ends after pause-tab rendering and needs gameplay helpers, event wiring, and update/render loop.
- `index.html`: DOM and data attributes for HUD, title/select, pause, dialogue, shop, ending screens, and mobile controls.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain, village, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, and Verdant Warden arena.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/touch input.
- `src/models.js`: Character definitions and procedural hero, enemy, NPC, and boss models.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- NPCs are Elder Elara (`kind: 'elder'`, at `(-4,-5)`) and Traveling Merchant (`kind: 'merchant'`, at `(5,-4)`); nearby collectibles include the waypoint and chest.
- Verdant Warden is near `(138,-78)`; world enemies include patrol/home, health, attack, aggro, cooldown, and dead fields.
- `createHero(id)` returns a rig with its root at `rig.rock`; character definitions are in `CHARACTERS` in `src/models.js`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`.
- Mobile action identifiers include `attack`, `heavy`, `jump`, `dodge`, `block`, `ability`, `ultimate`, `switch`, and `menu`; keyboard event wiring is still needed.

## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a playable anime-style 3D open-world action RPG, prioritizing a polished vertical slice.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, styling, shared utilities/input controls, procedural models, and procedural world.
- Implemented renderer, world setup, game state, hero mounting, resize handling, save/load, HUD, minimap, pause-tab content, and quest text in `src/game.js`.
- Added gameplay helpers for XP, dialogue, merchant shop, waypoint/chest/Starshard interactions, target selection, combat abilities, enemy damage, and defeat rewards.

### Active
- Wire UI flows and controls in `src/game.js`.
- Implement player movement/animation, enemy and boss behavior, camera, and render loop.
- Test the vertical slice, controls, interactions, combat, and persistence.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/game.js` with UI event wiring and input handling.
2. Implement player movement/animation, enemy and boss updates, camera, and render loop.
3. Run and test the project; fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Main integration; currently ends at line 269 after combat helpers, without final event wiring or game loop.
- `index.html`: DOM and data attributes for HUD, title/character selection, pause, dialogue, shop, ending screens, and mobile controls.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural terrain, village, NPCs, collectibles, enemy patrols, and Verdant Warden arena.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and keyboard/mouse/touch input.
- `src/models.js`: Character definitions and procedural hero, enemy, NPC, and boss models.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Repository files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- `createWorld(scene)` returns `world`, `npcs`, `enemies`, `bosses`, `collectibles`, `regions`, `sun`, and `getRegion(x, z)`.
- NPCs are Elder Elara (`kind: 'elder'`, at `(-4,-5)`) and Traveling Merchant (`kind: 'merchant'`, at `(5,-4)`); nearby collectibles include the waypoint and chest.
- Verdant Warden is near `(138,-78)`; enemies carry patrol/home, health, attack, aggro, cooldown, and dead fields.
- `createHero(id)` returns a rig with its root at `rig.rock`; character definitions are in `src/models.js`.
- `Input` exposes `down`, `pressed`, `mouseDown`, `mousePressed`, `actionDown`, `actionPressed`, `consumeLook()`, and `endFrame()`; mobile actions include `attack`, `heavy`, `jump`, `dodge`, `block`, `ability`, `ultimate`, `switch`, and `menu`.
- `AudioEngine.play()` effects include `swing`, `hit`, `heal`, `pickup`, `shard`, `roar`, `ult`, `death`, and `victory`.
- `ParticleSystem.emit()` supports configurable particle bursts via position, count, color, spread, speed, life, and related options.

## Requirements
- Include responsive movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice if full scope is too large.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, styling, procedural world and models, shared input/audio/particle utilities, HUD, minimap, pause tabs, quests, interactions, combat, enemy/boss behavior, and render loop.
- Added UI wiring for starting/continuing journeys, character selection, dialogue, shop, pause/settings, tonic use, save, respawn, and victory.
- `node --check src/game.js` completed without errors.

### Active
- Test the vertical slice in a browser, including runtime behavior, controls, interactions, combat, boss fight, death/respawn, and save/load; fix issues uncovered.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Run the app and check for browser console/runtime errors and visual issues.
2. Exercise start/continue, keyboard and mobile controls, interactions, combat, boss fight, death/respawn, and save/load.

- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and input controls.
- `src/models.js`: Character definitions and procedural hero, enemy, NPC, and boss models.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build ASTRA: REBIRTH as a polished, playable anime-style 3D action RPG vertical slice.
- Validate gameplay in a browser and fix runtime or interaction issues.

## Requirements
- Include movement, combat, enemies/bosses, exploration, progression, UI, stability, and visual polish.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls, persistence, and incremental testing.
- Use the existing technology and avoid unnecessary dependencies or oversized assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with the existing import map, locally vendored modules, and custom game modules.
- Prioritize a playable vertical slice over full scope.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, procedural world and models, input/audio/particle utilities, HUD, minimap, pause tabs, quests, interactions, combat, enemy/boss behavior, and render loop.
- Wired journeys, character selection, dialogue, shop, pause/settings, tonic use, save, respawn, and victory UI.
- Fixed Escape pause handling and dialogue keyboard advancement in `src/game.js`; added an inline SVG favicon in `index.html`.
- Browser-tested dialogue open/advance/close, merchant shop open/close, tonic purchase and persistence, enemy defeat/save/restore, mobile controls and ability action, and boss intro.
- Syntax checks pass for `src/game.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/models.js`, and `src/engine.js`; latest tests reported no page errors.
- Repository files are uncommitted and appear as untracked files.

### Active
- Validate and, if needed, fix end-to-end boss defeat and victory persistence.
- Run a final browser smoke test and syntax checks after any fixes.

### Blocked
- Boss victory has not been achieved in browser testing: with a level-20 Kael fixture, the boss health reached 13.47% after 12 ability attempts, but the victory screen and reward save were not triggered.

## Next Move
1. Investigate why boss attacks stop damaging or fail to finish the Verdant Warden; verify the attack target/facing and boss state in `src/game.js`.
2. Complete boss defeat, victory UI, and `bossDefeated`/quest/relic/gold save-and-restore validation.
3. Run final browser smoke tests and syntax checks.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Gameplay loop, UI wiring, persistence, combat, pause/dialogue handling.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world, NPCs, collectibles, enemies, and boss.
- `src/models.js`: Character, enemy, NPC, and boss models and boss definitions.
- `src/engine.js`: Audio, particles, utilities, and input controls.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- The local server responded HTTP 200 at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`.
- NPC positions: Elder Elara at `(-4, -5)`; Traveling Merchant at `(5, -4)`; Verdant Warden at `(138, -78)`.
- Boss activation requires `state.quest >= 2` and proximity within `boss.def.arena + 12`; Warden has 950 HP.
- `nearestEnemy()` uses hero facing and a forward-angle threshold; boss targeting may be affected by boss/player movement.
- Desktop enemy defeat increments kills and saves defeated enemy IDs; a reload restored the level successfully.
- Mobile ability action produced an enemy defeat in browser testing.
- Browser screenshots previously saved to `/tmp/opencode/astra-title.png` and `/tmp/opencode/astra-game.png`.
